grades.quote: If bit `[6]` of general register `rj` is `1` , it means that the content in `rj` is a large page (Huge Page) page table entry.
grades.reason: LoongArch LDDIR page-walk passage. It explains how a huge page is recognized during software walking (bit 6 of rj set means rj holds a huge-page entry). It does not describe how page size values are encoded in the TLB.

grades.quote: When the page size of the page table entry being filled is equal to the page size configured for STLB ( `CSR.STLBPS` ) it will be filled to STLB, otherwise it will be filled to MTLB.
grades.reason: LoongArch TLBFILL passage. It shows page size in TLB state: the entry's page size is compared with CSR.STLBPS to choose STLB or MTLB, and the size comes from CSR.TLBIDX_PS. It does not cover page-table walking or the encoding itself.

grades.quote: `PS` appears only in the MTLB. It is used to specify the size of the pages stored in this page table entry. The value is a power of `2` of the page size. That is, for a page size of `16KB` , `PS=14` .
grades.reason: LoongArch TLB entry format passage. It says MTLB entries carry a 6-bit PS field holding the power of 2 of the page size (16KB gives PS=14). STLB entries have no PS field and use CSR.STLBPS. This answers the TLB half of the query directly. It does not cover walking.
Generic operating-systems textbook text on TLB hierarchy and page-table walkers. It has no LoongArch content and says nothing about LoongArch page size representation.
